newsitem.title: USA: Coast Guard further restricts Mississippi traffic.
newsitem.headline: Coast Guard further restricts Mississippi traffic.

text.p: The Coast Guard on Friday placed further restrictions on Mississippi commercial traffic because of hazardous conditions on the river.
The latest restrictions will take effect Friday and apply to petroleum product and chemical cargoes, the Coast Guard said.

Notices to be sent out Friday afternoon "require that any tank vessel or tank ship 1,600 gross tons or more carrying certain oils and chemicals, as well as deep-draft chemical tank ships, downbound between mile 88 (New Orleans) to mile 233 (Baton Rouge), restrict travel to daylight hours," said petty officer Jason Maynard of the Coast Guard Marine Safety Office in New Orleans.
Commercial traffic on the river has been sharply cut back in recent weeks as the 1997 spring run-off has created the worst conditions in more than 60 years, according to shipping industry officials.

"We have never as an inudsutry had to resort to this level of safety on the Mississippi," said Ken Wells, vice president for the southern area of the American Waterways Operators, a Washington-based trade association representing cargo carriers.
"It is significantly slowing things down but there is enough concern for safety that noboday has been complaining," Wells added.
